item: 1 Drive module: subframe, lower jaw, drive arms and pivot
spec: 5 mm steel top plate about 295 x 400 mm with a notch round the jack's pump, welded hangers and brackets; 10 mm lower jaw with a packing bar that grips the donor yoke plate's rear edge with four M12 bolts (no drilling of the jack); two 10 mm steel drive arms each on its own 20 mm hollow tube pivot (4 mm wall, M12 bolt through the bore) behind the wheels, each with a spring tab
notes: Estimate for one prototype, laser-cut plate with welding; clamp fit depends on the donor yoke (R1 survey); about 10.6 kg; made constructable in PLP-DDR-003 (was $90); 5 mm top plate and hollow pivots carried into the model 2026-10-02 (PLP-DDR-003 A2); price unchanged

spec: 24 V brushless gearless hub servo motor, 200 mm (8 in) polyurethane or rubber tread, 12 N m or more continuous and 30 N m or more peak, fail-safe brake 20 N m or more dynamic, encoder, IP54 or better, about 7 kg
supplier: AGV hub motor maker (ZLTECH or UU Motor class)
notes: Per motor; class prices USD 165 (UU Motor SVB8S; 20/40 N m; 36 to 48 V; no brake listed) to USD 249 (ZLTECH 8 in 24/48 V; 40/80 N m); brake option and 24 V winding to confirm; TRL 2 figure of $170 was for a 16 N m class motor that is too weak

spec: Folded 2 mm aluminium box 270 x 300 x 96 mm with lid, cable glands, IP54; four riveted angle feet bolted to the top plate; height set so the donor handle clears it when lowered to horizontal
notes: Estimate; about 1.8 kg; feet added in PLP-DDR-003 (was $45); 1 mm deeper (96 mm) to sit on the 5 mm top plate

spec: 8S 25.6 V 20 Ah (512 Wh) LiFePO4, 8S6P 26650 cells in three layers about 270 x 115 x 85 mm, BMS 50 A continuous, charge temperature cut-off below 0 degC
notes: Estimate from retail 24 V 20 Ah packs; about 4.9 kg; 410 Wh usable at 80 % depth of discharge

spec: 24 V dual-channel brushless servo driver for the hub motors, 2 x 15 A continuous and 30 A peak, CAN, brake outputs, safe torque off and a monitored controlled-stop (stop category 1) input
supplier: AGV hub motor maker (sold with the motors)
notes: Estimate; match to the chosen motor's encoder and brake; safe torque off added to the specification for the ISO 3691-4 stopping function (no price change assumed; to confirm at the motor quote)

spec: 80 A main fuse at the pack terminal, two 24 V main contactors in series (each opened by one safety relay channel) with pre-charge resistor, lockable battery disconnect
notes: Estimate; second contactor (about USD 30) added for a dual-channel stop chain toward PL d (PLP-DDR-002; O6); about 1.1 kg

spec: ESP32-S3 class controller with CAN transceiver, UWB SPI links; dual-channel safety relay for the stop chain, taking the scanner's OSSD pair
notes: Estimate (controller about $25; safety relay about $60); firmware is not TRL 3 work

spec: Clamp-on head replacing the grip: thumbwheel throttle, belly-reverse paddle, mode key switch (walk or follow), horn button, beacon mount
22 mm red mushroom pushbutton, twist release, two normally closed contacts, yellow backing plate (ISO 13850 style)
notes: Per unit; one on the tiller head and one on the enclosure rear face

spec: Pressure-sensitive safety edge about 0.9 m in three lengths (front 480 mm and both sides) with evaluation unit, 40 mm compression travel at the front, on a 40 x 20 x 2 mm steel tube U hoop bolted to the subframe brackets with M8 rivet nuts
notes: Estimate; last stopping layer; about 2.3 kg with hoop; safety edge 68 mm high (60 to 128 mm above the floor) so the scanner shelf clears it

spec: Qorvo DWM3000 class UWB module on a carrier board: two on the bumper corners (450 mm baseline), one on the tiller head
24 V LED beacon on the tiller head, amber in walk mode and blue in follow mode, with travel buzzer
notes: Estimate; moved from the lid to the tiller head so the lowered handle clears the enclosure

spec: 16 mm steel cam shaft with two 22 mm eccentric cams and a crank, release link, 400 mm over-center lever of 20 x 10 x 2 mm steel tube with grip, two preload springs (about 100 N/mm, 34 mm outside diameter), two spring saddles and four slotted lift straps; raises the spring saddles and lifts the drive wheels about 10 mm clear of the floor
notes: Estimate; peak lever effort about 58 N (PLP-CAL-001 [G4]); made constructable in PLP-DDR-003 (was $20 for the lever and cam alone); lever now a steel tube (2026-10-02)

spec: Certified 29.2 V 5 A LiFePO4 charger, 100 to 240 V AC input
notes: Estimate; not modelled; stays at the charging point

spec: Belt tag with UWB module, rechargeable cell, stop button and vibration alert

item: 16 Handle angle sensor and gas spring
spec: Hall angle sensor on the handle pivot; gas spring that holds the handle upright in follow mode
10 AWG power cable, spiral wrap to the tiller head, connectors, fasteners, labels

Safety laser scanner for personnel detection (SICK nanoScan3 Core I/O class: 3 m protective field, 275 deg, 70 ms response, Type 3, PL d, SIL 2, 24 V, one OSSD pair, IP65, about 107 x 80 x 118 mm and 0.67 kg), on a 3 mm steel shelf bolted to the top of the bumper hoop's front bar, scan plane about 173 mm above the floor
supplier: Industrial automation distributor (SICK) plus local fabricator
notes: USD 3,444.30 scanner (NANS3-AAAZ30AN1, listed by Lesman) plus about USD 11 shelf; safety-rated, replaces the USD 69 RPLIDAR C1 class lidar (approved 2026-10-02: follow mode under ISO 3691-4); field set by the stopping calculation (PLP-CAL-001 S4); mounting holes, scan plane height above its base (about 40 mm) and response time to confirm at purchase

spec: Two 40 x 40 x 20 mm hard rubber blocks (about 80 Shore A) bolted under the top plate's front corners with two M8 bolts each; they meet the jack's frame head at 40 deg of steer, before any other kit part
notes: Added in PLP-DDR-003; stop angle set to the donor surveyed (R1)
